gap: No result ChatGPT got states that today the 3DMakerpro Seal costs $454 and the Seal Lite $215 at 3DMakerpro's US store. That puts the Seal $375 below the $829 Revopoint MINI 2 and $425 below the $879 Creality Raptor, ChatGPT's #1 and #3 picks. Even with 3DMakerpro's $199 multi-axis turntable, the Seal comes to $653, still under the MINI 2 alone.
standout_why: 3dprinting.com (cited) lists the Seal at about $699 and the Seal Lite at about $359, prices it says it researched on 2026-05-28 and 2026-06-01. It gives no total setup cost and no turntable prices. makermachinesatlas.com (cited) does not list the Seal or Seal Lite; its MINI 2 reference price is $746 and it says nothing about turntables in the box. print3dindex.com (cited) returned HTTP 403, so I could not compare against it. ChatGPT's own answers priced the Seal at $559.99 in one chat and '~$450–700' in another, and called the Seal Lite 'Budget under $400'. None of these pages has today's Seal price, the gap to the MINI 2 or Raptor, or the cost with a turntable.
decides: This supports Seal as the all-round pick for 10–300 mm objects. The maker's specs give both the Seal and the MINI 2 a 10 mm smallest object (from our page and 3dprinting.com), and the Seal claims 0.01 mm accuracy against the MINI 2's 0.05 mm. Today the Seal also costs $375 less. The MINI 2 keeps its edge only on point distance (0.02 mm) for 28 mm miniatures and jewelry. At $215, the Seal Lite becomes the clear budget pick, well below ChatGPT's 'under $400' bracket. The $879 Raptor and $1,999 Einstar Vega cost much more without a sourced small-object advantage.
